title: Velocity Sickness: What Happens When Your Whole Team Gets 10x Faster — Matt Dailey, Ref.
talk_summary: Matt Dailey argues that when AI makes implementation cheap, teams get 'velocity sickness': lots of PRs, agents sprinting in different directions, agent bankruptcy, and agents making critical decisions. His fix is to shift the core unit of work from ephemeral chat sessions to durable, shared plan docs that hold the decisions, so agents become stateless executors and humans own the decisions.

takeaways.technique: Plan doc as durable state, agent as stateless action
takeaways.what_they_do: They separate the agent (action) from a long-lived doc (state), so every agent starts from the same shared context instead of an isolated chat session, and humans can read the doc to recover context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: separate the the agent as the action and the doc as the state. And so, you can spawn new agents that have the same context

takeaways.technique: Move the review point earlier to the plan
takeaways.what_they_do: They align on key decisions up front in the plan doc, so code review becomes simpler because reviewers already know what matters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We've moved the the review point earlier into the process. So, we're aligning on the key decisions up front.

takeaways.technique: Shared plan doc enables parallel agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Because state is extracted into a shared doc, multiple agents can work from the same starting context in parallel without stepping on each other's implicit session state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you have this state extracted and you're working from a shared context, you get more parallel agents

takeaways.technique: Docs over chat for decision context
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue chat is isolated and ephemeral, so decisions made in chat vanish; docs bring forward the key decisions and act as a 'portal' to the relevant parts of the system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The problem with chats is that they are the relic of building for implementation. So they're they're default isolated and ephemeral

takeaways.what_they_do: They observe people planning and then not implementing, and treat that as a good sign: ideas get explored and only the worthwhile ones get built.
takeaways.evidence_quote: people start to plan and then not implement their plan. Uh and this is actually like a really good sign.

takeaways.what_they_do: They insist engineers must not let agents make critical decisions, or they lose ownership of the code and product.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you as an engineer are letting an agent make a critical decision, you are seeding control of your code
